data.objective: A premium sushi dining experience focused on fresh ingredients, handcrafted sushi and precise Japanese preparation.

data.rootCause: The render has strong source footage and a genuinely scroll-stopping hook, but the actual cut is undermined by obvious timeline duplication/holding, weak source continuity, and missing execution of the planned finishing devices. The CTA lands visually, yet the edit feels less like a finished premium commercial and more like a rough assembly because several beats repeat too long and the audio/feature audit indicates no visible text or motion refinement beyond the simplest lock-up.

issues.problem: The reel lingers too long on the bite reaction and then continues into repeated plate holds, which drains energy in a 13.5s cut.
issues.fix: Collapse the middle into one brief appetite reaction or remove it entirely; keep the edit moving from craft to hero plate without extended duplicates.

issues.problem: The timeline jumps across visually unrelated moments with weak transition logic, creating a stitched-together assembly feel instead of a premium sequence.
issues.fix: Use a more disciplined progression: flame -> ingredient prep -> slicing -> platter -> CTA, with each shot cut on action or reveal and no dead beats.

issues.problem: The render does not visibly/audibly reflect the planned commercial sound design; the audit shows only two SFX events and no speed ramps/transitions/text execution to support the cut.
issues.fix: Build a proper sound bed with torch, knife, plate, and CTA hits; ensure audio punctuates the hook and ending so the commercial feels finished.

issues.problem: The feature audit says text beats are zero, despite the rendered frames showing on-screen words. This suggests the type treatment is either inconsistent, poorly executed, or not reliably present throughout the render.
issues.fix: Make the typography intentional and minimal: one word at a time, safe placement, strong contrast, and no lingering duplicate CTA text beyond the final frame.

issues.problem: KAIRO branding is implied only through text; there is no real venue/signage/logo moment, so the brand feels generic rather than anchored.
issues.fix: If no logo shot exists, simplify the end card to a clean premium food CTA and keep the brand name highly legible and singular on the final hold.

issues.problem: The middle section broadens into multiple food ideas but does not deepen the premium dining story beyond craft and plating.
issues.fix: Sharpen the narrative to one promise: fresh ingredients + expert craftsmanship = craveable premium sushi worth visiting tonight.
